chapter.title: Chapter Five: Old Heads Know
chapter.subtitle: Every secret had a cost.
chapter.description: Bring the family to one table and hear the full rescue story.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: We had Sunday games planned before all this. We're keeping them. Then the family's staying for dinner.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You've got all of us here. Why wait?

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: Because I promised those people an afternoon, and because we're both too angry to finish a sentence right now.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: That's a good reason.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*It's the *only* reason. I've got about a hundred and I've used most of them on the *other* thing. But I'd like to finish one thing properly today, and I want to do it with somebody who's

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *going to be here in ten years*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(At the wall.)* You don't know that.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *(Not unkind.)*No. But you came *back*, and the *other* one came back, and I have two sons at a table, and if I spend the *whole* afternoon on *that*, then at some point in about a *year* one of

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: you is going to say "you never had a normal day with us," and it'll be *true*, and it'll be the *worst* thing anybody's said to me.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I'm staying for the answers. And if either of you leaves after the games, I'm coming after you, and I don't care what time it is, and I *will* come to the door.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm not leaving.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: You said that about something *else*, on a *rooftop*, in *July*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm not leaving.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I put the keys in Auntie's bowl. *(Beat.)* Everybody's remarkably available right now, and I'd like to *propose* that this is because nobody has *anything else* going on.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: Cornball.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I'm not saying it *bitterly*, I'm saying it *tactically*, because if two of these men were *available*, I'd be running a *different event*, and instead I got a *Sunday* with *seven matches* and a

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *grief* at the end, and honestly? It's a *good* Sunday. It's the *best* booking I've had in a *month*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Cornball, are you running a *funeral*?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I'm running a *Sunday*, champ. And the Sunday's got a *grief* in it, and everybody's got a *grief* in it, and that's *fine*, and I'm not going to be the man who stands up in the middle of

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: it and makes a bit about how *sad* everybody is. *(Beat.)*I've done that job for *nine years* and I'm *retiring* from it *today*, and the vacancy is *immediately* filled, but it wasn't by me.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, quietly, while he picks up the deck.)* I keep looking at him like he's going to disappear again.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(He heard it. He is close enough.)* He isn't leaving. *(Beat.)* Neither am I.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I'm next. *(Beat.)* Let me play before these two make me lose the whole afternoon to *staring*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You want company in the next one?

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Considering it properly, which she has never once done.)* *(Beat.)* Yeah. Stay.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: When he asks me if I'm *staying* — and he will, and he won't ask it *right*, because he doesn't know how to ask a question that isn't about himself — *(Beat.)*don't fix it for him. Let him be

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *bad* at it. *(Beat.)*It's the first *honest* thing I've watched him do in *four years* and it's going to be *awful*, and I want a *witness* who's going to let it be awful.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I didn't know you were playing today.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I play every Sunday. You don't know because you haven't been here.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Red told me the money was getting to you.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Okay.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: The messages I sent. The money was—

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Flat.)* I know what the money was.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: It paid for things. That's the whole thing and I want you to not look at me like it's more than that, because it *is* more than that, and that's the *point*. *(Beat.)*It paid for nappies and a car

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: seat and a *shoe*, and it did not *once* tell our child who their father was. That's the invoice. That's what the money *is*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: You don't know, because you think "I sent money" and I think "somebody sent money," and those are two *completely different* things, and it has taken me *four years* to be able to say the second

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: one out loud without crying in a *courtyard*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: What did you tell them.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: That you died.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You told my child I was *dead*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I told my child you *were*. *(Beat.)*And then I did something I'm not proud of, which is that it was *easier*. Because "your father is dead" is an *ending*, and an ending doesn't *call back*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*And then there was a *month* where I was glad about it, and I have never told anybody that, and I'm telling you, and I would like you to notice that I gave you the *worst* thing about me

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *first*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You gave me that first.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Why.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card.)* Because if I give you the *best* of me first, you'll spend the rest of the day managing *me*, and I've had four years of being managed and I am *so tired*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card.)* Champ, sit. It's our match.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* Can I ask you something and you can say no to.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I can say no to it.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Can I meet them.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* When I say.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Okay.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: First I need to know whether you're staying.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Staying where.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Staying *here*. Not tonight. *Here*. *(Beat.)* Not for a week. Not "I'll try." *Here*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I need it in a *sentence*, not a *word*. "Yes" is a word. What are you actually promising me.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I'm going to be at my door at seven-thirty every morning for a year, and if I'm not, you put a *chair* against it and you don't ask me why.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's the sentence. *(Beat.)* All right. You've got a year.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Nice finish. I needed ten minutes where I knew what I was looking at.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Gathering the deck.)* Can I—

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: No.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I didn't ask.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*You were *going* to. You were going to say "I want to meet them" again in a *different* tone, and I've had the *other* one, and it's a *good* one, and I'd like to keep the good one for

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *Tuesday*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Getting up.)*I'll tell you what they eat. *(Beat.)*You don't get the *whole* thing. You get one thing, and it's a *food*, and it's a stupid one, and if you get it right then we'll know what

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *else* you're paying attention to.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Okay.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(At the table, not turning round.)*It's pancakes. No syrup on them. Little cup on the side, because they're four and they think syrup is a *thing you add later*. *(Beat.)*Don't write it down. I'm

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *testing* you.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(To Cracked Head, low, after she has gone.)* Don't write it down. She's testing you. *(Beat.)* But *I* will.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Putting her deck down. Not shuffling. Not doing anything with it.)* Before my match. There's a thing and I want it said in front of people.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Wifey—

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I knew Blue gave Snitch the warehouse address.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I've known for a month.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You *what*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Dad told me. In his kitchen. He said he'd seen it since March and he hadn't said anything because it wasn't his. *(Beat.)*And I've had a *month*, Wifey. A month with a *head start*. And I didn't

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: do one thing with it, and you want to know why?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Why.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Because I *knew* how I'd use it. I'd have used it in about *nine seconds*. I'd have said it in the *first* row and I'd have made it about *me*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's the most *honest* thing you've said in a year and you said it while *taking my confession away*, and I want you to know that I notice.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I noticed too.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, not to Blue.)* And I'm only saying it out loud because you *asked* me, in a room, in *April*, with *no leverage*, and nobody has *ever* done that to me.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You said you already knew.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I knew I *couldn't* say it. That's different. *(Beat.)*I have been running the *records* of this family for four years. Every dollar, every sheet, every name. And I've been *holding* them, and I

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: called it *keeping things intact*, and last night a woman handed me a *page* and it turned out I hadn't kept *anything*. I've been standing in this building telling people the paperwork was fine.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: The paperwork is fine. *(Beat.)*That's the *problem*. I kept it fine *instead of* telling the truth, and the difference between those two things is the difference between a *binder* and a

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *person*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: What did you do with it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I let you come home and tell me it wasn't our business anymore. And then I helped Baby Momma plan a memorial. *(Beat.)*And then I made the *beds* and I packed the *nappies* and I did *forty* of

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: those, and I did them *well*, because I am *very* good at doing things *well* for people who have not *asked*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: That's a terrible thing to say about yourself.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's a *true* thing. *(Beat.)* Don't you dare make it a *bit*, Blue. If you make it a bit right now I will get up and leave and I *will not come back*, and I have *nothing* else to be doing.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *(Loud enough for the table and no further.)*Wifey. *(Beat.)*Whatever you're about to say, say it in the *present tense*. A thing that was *four years ago* has *people* in it now and they've all

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *grown*, and the only version that helps anybody is the one that says *what I did today.*

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat — and she redoes it, in the present tense, and it is much worse.)*Blue. I'm in your house right now. I know what you did. And instead of asking you about it *once*, I have gone downstairs

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: and done the *dishes* about it, every night, for *four years*, and I have let you believe that the dishes were what I was doing.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Take the other chair, champ. I'm done asking everybody to make this easier for me.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Good game. Baby Momma, I can still take the school run on Thursday if you want me to.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I need the help. I'm still angry with you.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Both is fine.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'll carry your things.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Not looking at him.)* They're right there. You don't need my permission to be useful.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Low, to Wifey.)* You said the difference between a binder and a person.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I did.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Which one are you?

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Beat — a long one — and she picks up her deck.)*Ask me in a year. *(Beat.)*And I want it to be a *rude* question, and I want it in *front of people*, and I don't want you to be *nice* about it,

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: because you being nice about it is the single most annoying thing you do.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: My turn. Nobody ask me to watch a pot while I'm at this table.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I put labels on the dishes.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: Why does my casserole say POSSIBLE EVIDENCE?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I lost track of which table we were using for what.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Holding it up, turning it.)* It's a *casserole*. It's got *corn* in it. It is the *least* probable piece of evidence in the *history* of this kitchen.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Genuinely aggrieved.)* It got *heated*. That's what happened. It got heated and I was *carrying* it and somebody *said something* and I did a *thing* with my *hand*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Cornball, my father's memorial program is in a *binder* labeled CASES.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Pulling a *second* label off a second dish with enormous dignity.)* Then that's the *first* one in the *series*.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: Peel it off. Both of them. *(Beat.)*And put the *binder* in the *middle* of this table where I can *see* it, because where I can't see a thing, that thing doesn't *happen* in my house, and I've

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: had *eleven years* of a thing not happening in my house.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card, mildly.)*You know what I do when the sisters start? I get the *potatoes* on the table early. *(Beat.)*Not because I love potatoes. Because a person holding a potato has *both

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: hands full* and cannot pick up a *fight*, and I have never lost an argument in my *kitchen* that I was *carrying a potato* in.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's the best thing I've ever heard.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: It's a *method*, baby.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: *(Collecting the win, mildly.)* You've got patience. That will take you further in this family than a winning streak.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Is there somewhere quiet I can talk to her after my match?

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: By the back table. *(Beat, and she does not look at him.)*And stop walking around with that recorder like you're waiting for the right *weather*. Nobody on this island is going to be talked into

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: something by a *machine*, and if she says no then she said *no* and the recorder's a *rude* thing to be holding.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's not for me.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: *(Sharply.)* Then what is it for.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: It's for *her*. She's had it since February and she hasn't opened it and I think she will today, and if she does, I'd like her to do that without me *holding* it for her.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: Then put it *there*, and let it be *hers*, and go and play your *cards*, and stop asking a *sixty-eight-year-old woman* for permission to *feel* something.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Side match? *(Beat.)* I got here early and everybody handed me something to carry.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Can you take this letter to the vending company?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Is it another appeal?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a *proposed settlement*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: How much is a settlement.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Three dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(To the player.)* It's three *dollars*, champ. I have carried *a chair* for less.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It has a *header*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Taking it, looking at it.)* Cornball, this is a *letter*. This is a letter about a *dollar*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It has *nine paragraphs*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Flipping through it.)* It has *four*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I've *lost* three. I lost three in a *courtyard* and I've accepted that.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Champ. Can I ask you a *serious* question and get a serious answer.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Go ahead.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: I've been moving cards through this tournament for three years. Not *in* it. *Through* it. And in three years I have moved about *four hundred* cards, and I have never once been asked to play,

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: because I'm the *courier*, and on this island the courier is a *thing that happens* and not a *person who plays*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You just asked me to play you. In Chapter One.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Yeah. I did. And you *won*, and I gave you the *tag*, and I've been *fine* about it, and I have been *fine* about it *every day*, and I want to say — out loud, in a courtyard, to a

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *stranger* — that it took me *three years* and a *tag* to be *invited*, and that everybody on this island thinks that's *normal*, and that it is *insane*, and that the only reason I'm saying it to

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *you* is that you *asked* me, which is *two* in nine years, and *one* of them was a *man who'd just met me* and I *remember* it.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Not writing. Not doing anything.)* Alley.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Don't.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I'm not *doing* anything. I'm not *writing* it down. *(Beat.)*I want to say that out loud, because I have a *clipboard* and I have *not* written it, and if anybody asks me later I *didn't write it

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: down*, and I want that to be *on the record* that I *chose* not to.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Side prize. Not part of the match. *(Beat.)* And I'd like you to take it and I want to explain it, and then I want you to be allowed to say no.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Go ahead.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Sunday. Not this one. Next Sunday, at eleven, the courier's yard has got four tables and nobody on them is invited to *anything*, it's just four men who carry things for a living, and we play.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*It is the only *free* thing left on this island and I would like to bring somebody who isn't a *businessman*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Why me.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Because you're the only person on this block who's ever *asked* a courier to sit down. And because you *lost* to me in Chapter Two. *(Beat.)*I want somebody there who *beat* me, so I can *lose*

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: again, and that's the only reason a man like me *invites* anybody.

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: I'm delivering the food and leaving the family to dinner.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: What about my letter?

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: Mailbox. End of the street. No opponent guarding it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, as Alley Runner walks off.)*Nine weeks ago he was moving cards and saying *nothing*, and now he's *asking* for a *thing* out loud, in front of a *crowd*, and he did it to *you*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I don't know what that is and I am *not* writing it down.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I brought all of them. *(Beat.)* Not just the one on the recorder.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: How many.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Nineteen.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Nineteen.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: In the first month. Then a gap. Then four more in the second year. Then — *(Beat.)*Then about two a year, and then nothing, and I've got the *dates*, and there's a *pattern*, and I'm not going to

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: explain the pattern because the pattern is that he *stopped*, and every one of them is a thing he decided not to do.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: (Flat.) The fourth one's a picture.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Of them *sitting down*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He asked how you were doing. I answered him, seventeen times. *(Beat.)* And I never once answered you.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Why didn't you ever *put these in with mine*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Because if I *gave* them to you, then you would have *asked me about them*. And if you asked me about them, then I would have had to *lie* to your face, every time, *for the rest of your life*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: And I knew I could hold the envelope. I knew I could hold it. *(Beat.)*And what I did not — and this is the thing I am actually saying, and I have never said it — what I did not *calculate* is

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: that you'd ask me *one more* time and I'd have to say *no again*, and that a woman can hear *the same no* twice and start *planning*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I planned in *March*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Beat.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I stopped asking you about money in March. I had a *spreadsheet*. I had a whole *page*, champ. *(Beat.)*And I couldn't *prove* a single thing on it, because you never *lied* to me — you never

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *once* lied to me, you just *didn't*, and I sat in my kitchen turning a *dollar* over for *four years* like it was a *stone*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Red. Did you want me to know.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(A long one.)* Yes.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Say that again.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Yes. In the beginning — for about *five months* — I wanted you to know, because I thought it would be a *relief*, and I thought I was protecting you from the *hiding*, and it turns out the hiding

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: was the *thing*, and I couldn't hand you the thing and stay clean at the same time, and I stayed clean because I *wanted* to be a good man, and I *was* good, and I have never *once* been good

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: about this.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I'm not going to say I'm not angry. I want that *said*, because everybody in this story is going to tell you I'm *noble* about it, and I'm not, and if I let them call me noble then I get to be

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *generous* and I don't *want* to be generous, I want to be *right*, and I want it to be *on record* that I chose the *right* over the *noble*, and it cost me *him*, and I'm going to have that.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: What do you want.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Gathering the messages. Not looking at him.)*The fourth one. That's all I need today. *(Beat.)*And I need to ask you something, and it's not a *favor*, it's a *job*, and I want you to actually

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *do* it and not *mean to*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Ask.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Take it to him. Not *tonight*. Not at the *roof*. *(Beat.)*Nine-fifteen tomorrow night. At my *door*. And you don't ring, and you don't knock, and you don't *call ahead* and you don't say it's

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *coming*, because if you *prepare* him then I'm doing the work again.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Nine-fifteen. At the door. *(Beat.)* I won't be in the car.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Red.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I *will* be in the car.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Fine.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I still haven't opened the page.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You said it was yours. Your name, your address, a call you've been putting off since March.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I did.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Are you going to make it?

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Ask me in September. *(Beat.)* And when I do it, you're the one who comes with me, and that's not a *favor* either, it's a *term*, and I have got about four of them.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: Last match before OG's table. I'm keeping us on time because Auntie threatened to serve cold food deliberately.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: I said I wasn't reheating it three times. Hear what I actually said.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: Terrifying either way. *(Beat.)* Champ, ready?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: No family revelation from you?

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: My family wants to know when I'm bringing the car back. *(Beat.)*That's *enough* pressure. My mother asks about the *car* on a *Sunday* and I have not had a *free* Sunday in *two years* because a

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: *vehicle* is not due back for *nine months* and nobody on *this island* will *accept* that as an *excuse*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: That's a *lease* problem.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: That's a *mother* problem.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat — and he means it.)*Champion, put that in your *clipboard*. A *mother* and a *car*. That's the *only* reason in this whole *yard* today that's got *nothing to do* with the *family*, and

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: it's the *best* one in the *book*.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: That's yours. OG's waiting. Take your time getting over there.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I've got time.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*You don't, though. You've got about four minutes, and there's a man at that table who's been waiting *all afternoon* to get a person in front of him, and he didn't ask for a *champion*,

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: he asked for a *witness*, and you know the difference, and I know you know it, because you've been the second thing for nine weeks.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(To the room, or to the chair.)*Both of you played here every Sunday until I turned the light off on you, and I want to say something about that before we start, and I've been *holding* it, and I

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: can *feel* myself not going to hold it much longer, so I'm going to say it now.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Low, to nobody.)* The light's off.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: He's been off since March.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Somebody should turn it on.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. *(Beat.)* Somebody should.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I've got a little left for one match. *(Beat.)*Then we're sitting down with the family, and I've asked for that and I'd like it to happen before I'm *tired*, because that's the whole thing and I'd

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: like to get it done.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: And eating. I swear some of you think dinner is an *optional chapter*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* After you.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I've forgotten how to do this.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You haven't. Your hands know.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*They do, don't they. *(Beat.)*Nine minutes, champ. Then I'll have to be a person instead of a man who's good at a card game. *(Beat.)*I have been *dreading* it for about *four years*, and

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: it is *worse* than the *funeral*, and I want that written down somewhere.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: Blue and Cracked used to play right here. Every Sunday. Right up until I turned the light off on them both.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: He never picked a side. He just picked winners.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You did favor him.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: I let you both stay up past every curfew on the calendar I made. That was the entire policy. *(He sets his deck down. It takes him a second to get it straight.)*I want to play this one. I promised

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: your guest a game and I'd like to finish one thing properly today, while I still can.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: While you still can what.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* After this, you ask me anything. All of it. I'm tired of sending people home with half an answer.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To you, low.)* He told me on Tuesday he'd give us the whole thing. I said that sounded like a funeral. He said it might be.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: Good game. Stay sitting. Both of you, come here.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I need to get this right, because I have gotten it wrong for four years to about twenty people and I am not doing it wrong one more time. That night, two men I had never seen were already on their

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: way to that warehouse. I got a call at eleven. I called the authorities. They got your brother out of there alive. He gave them the people above him. He has been somewhere safe ever since.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: And the memorial.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: And the memorial. Nobody told me to do that. Nobody put it in a contract. I made that decision at two in the morning by myself and I have made it every morning since.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: You said it to me twice.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: You don't get to say I know. That's the thing about you saying I know. You get to know that I was three weeks along. You made me stand up in front of that church and say it out loud so people

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: would stop asking, and then a week later you made me come back to your kitchen and say it again, to my face, because I asked you one question.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: You asked me if he'd called you. I said no. I said he'd never call you.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: He *had* called Red.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yes.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: So you looked at me and you lied with your whole chest and you let me plan a service.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I did.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I want you to know that I understood why. I want that written down somewhere, because I don't think people believe me. I understood it the second you said it. The people who were looking, the

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: danger, the child, all of it — I understood all of it and I forgave you for it in about four minutes. What I never got over is that you decided *for me*. You decided what I could handle. You

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: decided I was a person who takes bad news standing up, and so you never once had to ask me if I could.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(He looks at the table for a long moment.)*I told myself I was keeping you safe. Every day for four years I told myself that. And it got easier every single time I said it, which is how I know it

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: was a lie. If it had been true it would have gotten harder.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I'm not going to ask you to forgive me tonight. I want that understood. I'm sixty-eight years old and I know exactly how long I've got, and I'm not spending whatever's left on asking people for

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: something they don't owe me.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Flat.)* You knew about the address.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I knew somebody had put out a location. I never knew who.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I gave it to Snitch.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Don't. Don't tell me not to. I gave Snitch the address four years ago. I told him where the handoff was, I told him to bring a camera, and I told myself I was going to get somebody to finally see

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: what you were doing, because I was tired, because I was your little brother your entire life, because every room on this block went quiet when your name came up and not one single room has ever

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: gone quiet for mine—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I knew those men were on their way. I want that said out loud in this room, because Dad is going to want it said out loud. I knew what I was handing you and I handed it anyway. I didn't think

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: anybody would get hurt. *(Beat.)*Write that down. I didn't think anybody would get hurt. And then cross it out, because I did think it. I thought about it for two days and then I did it anyway.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: Blue—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You *stood up there*. *(He stands. Nobody tells him to sit.)*You said the words. You looked at me and you said "your brother is gone" and I believed you, and I hated him for leaving. I hated him

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: for four years. I sat in that chair and I cried about a man who was alive because you told me he wasn't.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: I know what I took.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You took my brother and you gave me a shirt.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I'm not mad at you.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Don't do that.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I'm not mad at you, Blue. I'm not mad at you because I have not sent you one single thing. Not a call. Not a birthday. Not a dollar. Not a word. Every one of them went to Red, and I told myself I

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: was keeping you safe, and I was, but that wasn't why, and we both know it. I was protecting me. Because if I picked up that phone and you said "we thought you were dead" then I would have had to

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: come back and live in it. So no. You do not get to be the worst person in this room tonight. I've had four years to be the worst one and I was worse than you, because you did yours in a single

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: night and I have been doing mine every morning for four years and I'm still doing it right now, in this chair, telling you I'm not mad, when the honest thing to say is that I am so mad at you I

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: can't eat.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I wasn't trying to be worse.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I know. That's what makes it stupid. You did it stupid, in one night, out of jealousy, and I did it smart and slow, for years, with a whole plan, and I got the same result. We should be so much

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: worse at this.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Can the two of you stop talking to each other and look at me.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I have been very good this season. I want that on the record with everybody in this room. I played in every one of these. I sat at tables with men who were talking about my family and I passed the

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: salt. I let Snitch stand three feet from me with a phone for six weeks and I never once raised my voice in public about any single one of you. So when I tell you what happened in this family, I

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: need you to hear it coming from a person standing in front of you, and not from a video, and not from something Snitch posts with a caption about it.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Neither of you lost anybody. I know how that sounds. I am not being cruel, I am being accurate, and I need it to be accurate because I am the only person in this room who spent four years raising

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: a child who did not have a father. You lost a man for four years. I lost the man who was supposed to come home. Those are not the same sentence and they were never going to be the same sentence,

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: and I have been hearing the other one at every table for six weeks.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I am not deciding anything tonight. I want that in the record too. I am not deciding anything tonight, and I want everybody at this table to understand that is not me being kind. That is me buying

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: myself one night where I do not have to be the reasonable one in front of my son in the morning.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(He starts to say something.)* Baby Momma, I—

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: You will get your turn. You had four years and a church and a man on a stage to say it to me. I have had one afternoon. *(Beat.)*I'm going to go eat now, and I'm going to sit next to my son, and

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: if you want to say something to me you can say it where he can hear it, because I'm done protecting him from this family.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: That's fair.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: Food's up! Everybody who wants a plate with a hot dinner in it, this is the last call. I'm not doing a second round.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: She's right. About all of it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Don't be nice to me.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I'm not being nice. I'm being tired. We're all being tired. *(Beat.)* Go eat, Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: In a minute.

tips: Continue the story at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Not looking up.)* Plating for eleven. I always plate for eleven. God knows how many show up, I cook what the Lord provides, I am not running a headcount out here like it's a fire drill.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(To Wifey, pointing.)* You. You're on the good table. Don't argue, there's a reason, I can't explain the reason.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I'm perfectly happy at the—

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: I said the good table.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Already moving.)* Yes ma'am.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Hands over a dish.)* Before anybody say anything — I know. I know. I got a *lot* of cheese.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: That is not cheese, that's a *situation*.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: It's a aged cheddar situation. It's an artisan situation. It's got a *name* on the side. The name's a man, I met him at a market in March, his name is Terrence, Terrence is not a businessman,

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Terrence is a dreamer, and I have given this man my rent money.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Serving.)* You have given this man three hundred dollars and he gave you a wheel of store-brand cheddar and a handshake.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: A *long* handshake.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Not looking up.)* Put it in the green bowl, not the blue, the blue's for the salad and I don't need a cheese incident before I bless this food.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Yes ma'am.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Cornball.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I know. I know. I put that on in a moment of *panic*, Wifey, and then I forgot, and now I can't take it off 'cause I think the *adhesive* is part of the record.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: It's part of the record. Leave it. Let OG eat the evidence.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(Carrying a tray, narrating.)* And here's the man of the hour. Man of the hour! Didn't bring a speech, though. Brother, you got all night to write one and you showed up with a *dish*.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: It was already in the sink.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: It's a metaphor, it's a *dish* metaphor, I'm workshopping—

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Roaster.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: Yeah?

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: You got a plate and you got a bit, and one of them is what's keeping you in this family.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: —and I told him the chairs were accounted for, and he says account for 'em again like I don't run a—

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Flat, corporate, the other one.)* Promoter's fine. Promoter's business. I'll handle the count tomorrow.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: You're not even talking about Promoter.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I'm always talking about Promoter.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: There's still the tournament.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: There's still the tournament.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: You ran it four years. You built it. And the second I walk in you act like I'm visiting something you own.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(The business voice, already slipping.)* I have kept that event *functioning*—

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: You kept it functioning like a parking garage. I get a *courtesy* of the tournament I used to win.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Nobody says that on this block. I want to say that. Nobody on this block says that to me, and not because of you, Cracked.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know what everybody on this block think I am right now. I been hearing it all day, I been hearing it since this morning. I got a brother come back from the dead and a whole street that think I'm

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: the villain in it, and I can't even be mad about it, 'cause what you *say* on that porch is truer than what I been telling myself for four years. So I'm just gon'— I'm just gon' eat.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(To himself, still cutting.)*See, this is what I been saying. This whole event is being held together with folding chairs and one man who can't see the bottom of the cake.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(He sets the plate down.)*And I don't got a problem with that. I got a problem with the *pie*. Somebody moved that pie. I been watching that pie all night.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: I moved the pie.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: To where?

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: I moved the pie to the *cold*.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(A beat, genuinely wounded.)* Church, we been through a lot tonight. The pie was right there.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(To nobody, too loud.)* Who moved my pie. I *swear* to God.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Beat. She's been watching the plate the whole time.)* Cornball.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Doesn't turn around.)* I got it.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: Leave it there.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(To the room, and she's not managing a room anymore.)*Y'all can talk about the tournament after we eat. I didn't cook for a *hearing*. I cooked because it's Sunday and this is where the people I

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: know eat, and I would like to have one meal where nobody's being brave.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Quieter, to Baby Momma only.)* I set it every week. It's habit. Don't make it a thing.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: Mm. *(Beat.)* Eat.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I'm going home after I eat. And I'll decide when we talk again.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Flat, and she does not look at him.)*You don't know, you just said it so I'd stop. I'm telling you: don't come to my door with Snitch. I don't want to watch y'all rehearse it. I got four years

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: of not knowing and I will be *very* clear when I'm done not knowing.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: That's fair.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: It ain't fair. Nothing about this is fair. Fair is a word for people who got options.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: Then what is it?

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: It's the card game. *(Beat.)* You know how it works. Somebody somebody. You don't get a rematch till the other one says so.
